Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the second innings to start! Bangladesh are out to chase 135 in 20 overs. It's Litton Das and Rony Talukdar to open the batting for the visitors. Tim Southee to start the attack for New Zealand. Let's Play!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

The stage is set for an enthralling pursuit, with the Bangladesh batters looking to capitalize on their bowlers' splendid performance. On the other hand, New Zealand's bowlers aim to conjure a magic trick to defend their total and stage a comeback. The upcoming innings promises intense moments and a captivating battle between bat and ball, leaving fans on the edge of their seats in anticipation of the unfolding drama. Stay tuned.

James Neesham is in for a chat. He says that it was hard to get a read on the bounce of the surface. Adds that it was tough to play cross-batted shots. Mentions that the new ball was skidding on. Shares that this total is less than what they were targeting but it is definitely defendable. Feels that if they get a couple of early wickets early on, they can have a chance. Says that he is looking forward to Ben Sears bowling on this surface. States that all of the players in their side have played enough cricket to set up a defendable total and hopes that it is what they have done.

The prowess of the Bangladesh bowlers was on full display, led by the strategic acumen of their skipper, Najmul Hossain Shanto. The bowling unit executed their plans immaculately, stifling the New Zealand batters from the outset. Shoriful Islam emerged as a standout performer, claiming 3 wickets, in which the first two came in his first over. Mahedi Hasan and Mustafizur Rahman contributed with 2 wickets each. Tanzim Hasan Sakib made a memorable T20I debut by securing his maiden wicket. The collective bowling effort by Bangladesh showcased precision and control, providing them with a significant opportunity to seize an early advantage in the series with a 1-0 lead. As the action shifts to the second innings, Bangladesh faces the task of chasing down 135 runs in 20 overs. The favorable conditions and a well-behaved pitch suggest that the target is within reach.

The conclusion of the first innings in the inaugural T20 match of the three-game showdown between New Zealand and Bangladesh unfolds a gripping narrative. The hosts, New Zealand, found themselves in a challenging position as they faced a stern examination by the Bangladeshi bowlers. Opting to bat first, New Zealand struggled to find a substantial partnership, managing a total of 134 runs while losing 9 wickets in their allocated 20 overs. The top order, unfortunately, failed to make significant contributions, with 19 runs being the highest individual score among the top five batters. The lone standout partnership emerged between James Neesham and Mitchell Santner, adding 41 crucial runs before Santner's dismissal. Neesham, however, played a valiant innings, scoring 48 off just 29 balls to provide a glimmer of hope for his side. Contributions from the lower order eventually propelled New Zealand to cross the 130-run mark.

OUT! LBW! Fantastic review from Najmul Hossain Shanto and Bangladesh! A perfect in swinger from a fuller length on the line of the stumps. Glenn Phillips has no idea where the ball is, and he looks to leave it alone. The ball hits him on the front pads with no shot offered. A massive appeal for LBW but turned down. Shoriful Islam is pretty convinced and Najmul Hossain Shanto takes the review. The Ball Tracking shows that the ball has pitched in line, the impact is around middle and the ball goes on to crash into the middle stump. Glenn Phillips has to walk back. What a start for Bangladesh.

Finn Allen still playing for the in swinger, looking to drive the ball on the up, gets a thick outside edge and the ball carries to Soumya Sarkar standing at a widish second slip. New Zealand in early trouble.

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the pre-game formalities and it is now time for the action to get underway! The two umpires make their way out to the middle followed by the Bangladesh players. It will be Finn Allen and Tim Seifert to open the innings for New Zealand. Bangladesh are starting with spin in the form of Mahedi Hasan. Let's play...

We are moments away from the first ball in this series opener but before that, the match officials and the two teams will line up for the national anthems. It will be Bangladesh's national anthem first followed by the national anthem of New Zealand.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Najmul Hossain Shanto (C), Soumya Sarkar, Litton Das (WK), Rony Talukdar, Towhid Hridoy, Afif Hossain, Mahedi Hasan, Tanzim Hasan Sakib (On T20I debut), Mustafizur Rahman, Shoriful Islam, Rishad Hossain.
New Zealand (Playing XI) - Tim Seifert (WK), Finn Allen, Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Mark Chapman, James Neesham, Mitchell Santner (C), Adam Milne, Tim Southee, Ish Sodhi, Ben Sears.
TOSS - Bangladesh have won the toss and they have elected to BOWL first.

On the flip side, Mitchell Santner assumes the role of captaincy for New Zealand, entrusted with leadership duties in the absence of regular skipper Kane Williamson. New Zealand asserted their dominance in the ODI series, clinching a 2-1 victory with commendable performances in the first two encounters. However, the third ODI witnessed a stunning twist as the hosts faced embarrassment, being bowled out for 98 runs. But coming into this series the Black Caps' batting lineup remains formidable, featuring talents like Finn Allen and Daryl Mitchell. Rachin Ravindra too enters the game in outstanding form. In the bowling department, the responsibility rests on Adam Milne, Ish Sodhi, and Tim Southee to maintain the momentum. The skipper himself is in great form with the ball.  The battle for supremacy promises to be fiercely contested, and cricket enthusiasts worldwide can anticipate thrilling encounters as these two sides vie for T20I glory. Stay tuned with us for the upcoming toss and lineup updates.

Najmul Hossain Shanto continues to lead the charge for Bangladesh, his captaincy gaining credibility with each match. The Tigers' remarkable win in the final ODI showcased their ability to tackle the challenging conditions and opposition, bowling New Zealand out for a mere 98 runs, and then chasing down the target with just the loss of one wicket, securing a memorable win and instilling a fresh wave of confidence as they step into the T20I series. Bangladesh, fueled by Litton Das and Soumya Sarkar, will be eager to make a mark in the T20 series.  In the bowling department, the likes of Mustafizur Rahman, Shoriful Islam, Hasan Mahmud, and Tanzim Hasan Sakib bear the responsibility. Their clash with New Zealand's seasoned batting lineup adds an intriguing dimension, testing their mettle against a formidable opponent.

A warm greeting to cricket enthusiasts around the globe! As the New Zealand vs. Bangladesh series transitions to the enthralling world of T20 cricket, the stage is set for an exhilarating contest at McLean Park, Napier. This picturesque venue is renowned for its batting-friendly wicket, offering batters an opportunity to showcase their skills once they find their groove. With a history of high scores in T20s at this venue, fans can anticipate another run-filled spectacle, making the toss-winning captain's decision to bowl first a tantalizing strategic move.
... MATCH DAY ...

After an unexpected end to the ODI series, it is now time for New Zealand and Bangladesh to clash in a T20I series. This three-match series holds significant importance for both sides as part of their preparations for the 2024 Men's T20 World Cup in the West Indies and the USA. McLean Park in Napier will play host to the series opener, where Bangladesh will have fond memories of their first-ever ODI win against New Zealand in New Zealand, whereas the Kiwis will look to put that loss behind them and start afresh. In the absence of the designated skipper, Kane Williamson, Mitchell Santner has been handed the reigns for the T20I series. The hosts are packed with a plethora of all-rounders, with Daryl Mitchell, Rachin Ravindra, James Neesham, and Glenn Phillips in their ranks. Finn Allen and Tim Seifert have retained their places at the top of the order, as has Mark Chapman in the middle order. Ish Sodhi will perform the spin bowling duties alongside Mitchell Santner, while Tim Southee will spearhead the pace attack. Kyle Jamieson has also been rested for this series, but Santner has Adam Milne, Jacob Duffy, and Ben Sears as the other pace bowling options at his disposal. On the other hand, Najmul Hossain Shanto's Bangladesh will take the field with the aim of creating more history on this tour as they eye their first-ever T20I series win on New Zealand soil. Other than Shanto, Litton Das, Soumya Sarkar, and Towhid Hridoy will have to step up with the bat. Like the hosts, the visitors also have a good bunch of all-rounders in Mehidy Hasan, Mahedi Hasan, Afif Hossain, and Shamim Hossain. Shoriful Islam and Tanzim Hasan Sakib were the architects of their win in the third ODI, and the duo will be hoping to deal more damage, as will Mustafizur Rahman. In the previous bilateral T20I series held in New Zealand between these two sides, the Kiwis dished out a 3-0 hammering. Also, Bangladesh are yet to register a T20I win against New Zealand in New Zealand. Will the tourists spring a surprise at Napier again? Or will it be New Zealand who take the lead in the series? We will find out soon enough.
